Results.ReviewText: The Weber Spirit E-310 reminds me of the 90s Weber Genesis in every positive way possible. It's a grill that inspires confidence in those less serious about grilling, but still provides the functionality demanded by a seasoned Pro. It's incredibly simple to use, clean, and maintain just like the Genesis of the 90s. The Spirit E-310 is also the perfect size; it offers great cooking real-estate and enough room to establish cooking zones, without being massive and heavy. If you need to move it, with no tank and the side tray folded it's a one-person-carry. While there are several more highly optioned variations of this generation Spirit, you can't go wrong with this one; it's the perfect grill to just go out, and cook. My only wish is that there were more fun color options like the 90s Genesis models (I know there are some but they're not readily available). I grew up helping my Dad grill on a Genesis 1000 that was a beautiful burnt orange color and would've loved something like that. @Weber maybe add paint to sample to the "build your own Weber" page? Lol
Results.Title: 90s Throwback

Results.ReviewText: I think the grill components are good quality. That said I have some complaints.  Weber doesn’t offer you an easy way to move the grill. It has wheels but the only way to move it is to lift up a flimsy folding table on one end of the grill. Unless you grab it by the very end of that table and lift upward, putting pressure on the hinges, it will pop out of the pins and be a wobbly mess. I could see even getting injured because of this. I also do not find the porcelain grills to be very nonstick, and they stain very easily. The gas system design I also feel is lacking, because my old grill didn’t care which burner I turned on first, but this one you have to turn on the far left one first and light that, and then you can turn on the ones to the right of it. If you don’t know this, and try to light one of the other two first by mistake, you can have a dangerous buildup of gas which could explode when you light it.

ClientResponses.Response:
Thank you for your feedback. We are very sorry to hear your grill is not getting hot. We are here to help. 

It sounds like you may be activating a safety device built into the regulator. This safety device is a component of all LP gas regulators and is designed to reduce the flow of gas in the event of a leak.

You can inadvertently activate the safety device without having a gas leak. Typically, this occurs if you do not wait a sufficient time between opening the tank valve and the burner control knobs or if one or more of the burner control knobs is in an open position when opening the LP tank valve. When the safety device has been activated the grill is referred to as being in “bypass”.

Keep in mind that the safety device reacts to gas leaks. If a grill is in bypass, the gas connections and hose should be tested for leaks with a soap and water solution.

If you do activate the gas regulator safety device, the grill may struggle to reach high temperatures or may not light at all, even with all burners on the START/HIGH setting.

To ensure that you are not inadvertently activating the safety device as you turn on the grill, please use the following procedure:

-Turn all burner control knobs to OFF, including the side burner control knob if present.

- Visually confirm all burners are extinguished (no flame present) 

-Make sure the grill lid is open. Open the LP tank valve and then wait at least 60 seconds. This will allow the hose and regulator to pressurize.

-Turn the appropriate burner control knob for your model grill to the START/HIGH position and then ignite the grill by pushing the ignition button.

-Turn each of the other burner control knobs to high, one at a time, and press the igniter button (if applicable for your model). Repeat this process until all the burners have been lit.

-Close the grill lid.

-The grill should reach approximately 500 to 550 degrees in 10-15 minutes.

When you are done grilling:

-Turn all burner control knobs to the OFF position

-Turn off the LP tank valve last.

Our Care team is reaching out to help. Please look for our outreach soon. Thank you!
ClientResponses.Name: Weber grills

Results.ReviewText: If this is the standard for propane grills in 2023, I feel ripped off.  This grill is a WEAK, literally low-energy time waster.  If your gig is firing up some hot dogs and hamburgers [not too thick], you're good to go.  Not sure if you can toast the rolls, not enough heat.  I'm flabbergasted how this passes for a outdoor grill.  The heat source is too far away from the cooking surface, the "flavorizer bars"  are like a heat sheild.  Why would you cover the flame so thoroughly?  I have read and re-read the troubleshooting guides thinking I had tripped the safety mechanism.  Is 20 times too many to make sure?  I replaced the regulator, I have tried multiple propane sources.  And yet this grill is no match for my Air Fryer in term of performance.  Nothing like grilling a whole chicken for 90 minutes @ 400F and it comes out under cooked and soggy.  Good luck trying to sear something on this low energy dud of a grill.  Perhaps I have much higher expectations than most folk.  I want  a grill that is so robust that you have to tame the flame, not hope you can get your meal cooked.  Now I'm stuck with this monolith of mediocre engineering lurking on my deck and I hate it.
Results.Title: mediocre waste of money

We appreciate your feedback. We are very sorry to hear your regulator is leaking. We are here to help. 

In almost every case of reported leaks, the rubber gasket on the inside of the propane tank nozzle is oval in shape, as opposed to round, is cracked or is otherwise compromised, and therefore results in a leak. The gasket should be perfectly round, with no nicks or cracks.

Our Care team is reaching out to assist you further. Thank you!
